For `x₀ : ℝ` and `delta > 0`, the neighbourhood is `U(x₀, delta) = { x | x₀ − delta < x < x₀ + delta }`; the punctured neighbourhood removes the centre, `U°(x₀, delta) = { x | x₀ − delta < x < x₀ + delta ∧ x ≠ x₀ }`. Equivalently `x ∈ U(x₀, delta) ↔ |x − x₀| < delta`, and `U°(x₀, delta) ⊆ U(x₀, delta)`.

Every epsilon-N and epsilon-delta statement below is phrased as membership in a neighbourhood. That formulation survives the move to metric and topological spaces, whereas the inequality `|a − L| < epsilon` is bookkeeping specific to ℝ.
